Share on X Telegram The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has assured Nigerians that the ballot papers to be used for Saturday’s nationwide mock accreditation exercise will not bear the names of any registered political parties.
INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance on Wednesday during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory in Abuja.
Amupitan said the ballot papers would be pseudo-ballot papers designed solely for the simulation, dismissing concerns that the exercise could provide an opportunity for electoral manipulation ahead of the 2027 general elections.
“The ballot papers to be used are pseudo-ballot papers and not containing the name of the registered political parties,” he said.
He added that the absence of political party names would be visible to participants and members of the public.
According to the INEC chairman, the mock accreditation will be conducted in two polling units per ward nationwide and will serve as an operational test of the commission’s electoral infrastructure and processes.
He said the exercise would particularly assess the upgraded Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS), logistics arrangements and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).
Amupitan explained that the simulation would test the transmission and verification of election results, alongside measures introduced to strengthen the credibility of the result management process.
He disclosed that under the commission’s improved IReV protocol, figures entered by presiding officers on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before being uploaded to the portal.
He said the measure was designed to ensure that results transmitted from polling units were accurate and verified by stakeholders present before upload, thereby reducing ambiguities associated with manual collation.
The INEC chairman directed the RECs to ensure effective supervision of the exercise, disclosing that national commissioners had been instructed to return to their respective zones to monitor the process.
He added that he would personally monitor the exercise in the field, while all RECs were expected to oversee preparations in their respective states and submit comprehensive technical audit reports by Monday.
On preparations for the 2027 general elections, Amupitan charged the RECs to ensure the effective implementation of the commission’s plans, warning that the electoral timetable left little room for delays or prolonged deliberations.
He described the RECs as the commission’s chief operational officers at the grassroots, stressing that the credibility and public acceptance of the 2027 elections would depend largely on their vigilance, neutrality and administrative efficiency.
Amupitan urged them to build on lessons from recent off-cycle elections and the commission’s zonal readiness assessment meetings, noting that the general elections would involve significantly greater operational demands.
He said INEC was managing a verified register of more than 100 million voters and would deploy BVAS devices alongside over 1.4 million ad-hoc personnel across the country.
According to him, the exercise would cover diverse locations, including densely populated urban centres, remote riverine communities, insurgency-affected areas and locations hosting internally displaced persons.
He warned that even minor administrative failures in any state could attract nationwide attention and undermine public confidence in the commission’s preparedness.
The INEC chairman also disclosed that the commission had commenced the distribution of sensitive and non-sensitive election materials to states.
He consequently urged the RECs to address operational challenges, communication gaps and logistics difficulties identified during reviews of recent off-cycle elections.
Amupitan further stressed the need to prioritise inclusivity and proper documentation of electoral processes as part of efforts to strengthen public confidence in the 2027 general elections.
